summary: How radar finds targets: timing, power and wavelength math, the main parts, and Figures 8A1 to 8A8.

blocks.title: Echo timing
items: A pulse goes out, an echo returns, and the wait gives the range. The antenna's direction gives the bearing.
Range constant: 150 meters per microsecond: 300 m per µs ÷ 2 for the round trip.
1 RADAR mile = 12.34 µs, out and back. One way: 6.17 µs, so 3 nm takes 18.51 µs.

blocks.title: Range, power and bands
items: Echo size: transmitted power, antenna effective area, transmit and receive losses, RADAR cross section, range to target.
Recovery time has no effect on maximum range.
Minimum range is set by transmitted pulse width.
Average power is measured over a period of time. For peak, divide it by duty cycle.
Pulses: short range, narrow, fast rate. Long range, wider, lower PRR. Small targets, long, high output power.
Microwaves give stronger target echoes. Marine radar is SHF.
Wavelength: λ = c ÷ f. 3 GHz: 10 cm.
S-band: 2 to 4 GHz, less affected by weather.
X-band: 8 to 12 GHz, better bearing resolution.

blocks.title: Components
items: Silicon crystals: static-sensitive, stored in lead foil, low current, typically 3 mA.
Magnetron filament: carries dangerous voltages.
Gunn oscillator: resonant cavity sets the frequency; uses negative resistance and bulk effect.
Reflex klystron: cavity dimensions set the frequency; repeller voltage fine-tunes.
Blocking oscillator: T = R × C. Phantastron: a linear ramp when externally triggered.
Sample-and-hold: analog switch, capacitor, amplifiers, input and output buffers.
Not an analog-to-digital method: dynamic-range conversion.
TTL and CMOS NAND: both have active pull-up. At high frequencies, CMOS uses almost TTL's power.

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: Meters, not yards. 150, not 300.
Duty cycle: ignore peak power and range.
PRF answers are always or less.
PRR means the magnetron, not the local oscillator or klystron.
